7_real_production_timings.source: Real conversations observed live during this bench session 2026-04-25. The robot_brain.log was truncated when robot_brain restarted between iterations; n=10 round-trips below were captured from operator terminal output across 4 conversation episodes.

round_total_ms_full_pipeline.note: Includes audio playback wait. Most of the 8.7 s p50 is the robot SPEAKING the response, not waiting before speaking.

llm_ttfb_ms_streaming.note: First TTS chunk fires at this latency in real conversation.

llm_wall_ms_includes_audio_playback.note: wall_ms = LLM stream end + speaker.wait_and_stop(). Dominated by audio playback time (TTS-paced speech).

caveats: STT: measured on synthesized speech via edge-tts. Real human speech with similar clarity should be comparable; noisy / accented speech may be 2-3x slower.
Mem0 search: measures embed + Qdrant retrieve. Cold cache (first query) is 10-20x slower than warm.
LLM TTFB: measured on the production-mirroring prompt (~1500 tok system+history). Shorter prompts will be faster.
TTS first-byte: time from request to first audio CHUNK arriving at robot_brain. NOT time-to-user-hears. Add ~100-300 ms for WebRTC + audio buffer pipeline before sound reaches the speaker.
WebRTC RTT: ICMP ping is a lower bound on network round-trip. Real WebRTC audio frame RTT is 30-80 ms (NAT traversal, encryption, jitter buffer overhead).

Sum-of-stages 'estimated TTFB' is a theoretical lower bound for an ideal pipeline. Real production wall-clock is higher due to sequential dependencies the bench does not capture (audio playback wait, etc). Real production times reported separately below.

budget_theoretical_lower_bound_ms.note: This is theoretical (sum of independent measurements). Real production p50 round-trip is 9.4 s and LLM TTFB p50 is 728 ms — see 7_real_production_timings.

headline.honest_summary: On a robot voice stack with 2× RTX 3090 + vLLM AWQ + Mem0 + edge-TTS + WebRTC: real-world LLM TTFB p50 is 728 ms (about cloud-agent territory). Total round-trip p50 is 9.4 s but ~7 s of that is the robot SPEAKING the reply, not waiting to start. The 'instant-response' window (user finishes -> robot starts speaking) is well under a second.
